wu: Greetings and Name Chain: Students stand in a circle, one student says 'Hello, my name is [name]', the next repeats the name and adds their own, continuing around the circle to review personal introductions.
wuAlt: Interview Bingo: Students mingle asking 'What's your name?' and 'Where are you from?' to fill a bingo grid with classmates' names.
Flashcard Quick Review: Teacher holds up flashcards of S1 topics (food, shopping, directions) and students shout the English word.
pres: Teacher distributes the S1 written paper (35 min) with clear instructions, modeling the first question on the board to ensure understanding before students begin individually.
presAlt: Oral Exam Demo: Teacher conducts a short mock speaking interview with a volunteer student, showing the format and questions to the class.
S1 Topic Review: Teacher uses a mind map on the board to recap all S1 vocabulary and functions (greetings, shopping, etc.).
prac: While waiting for their speaking slot, students complete a 'Find Someone Who...' worksheet with S1 topics (e.g., 'Find someone who likes coffee'), practicing question forms in pairs.
pracAlt: Vocabulary Matching: Students match S1 words (e.g., 'apple', 'bread') to pictures on a worksheet, working in pairs to check answers.
Error Correction: Teacher writes 5 S1 sentences with errors on the board; students work in pairs to find and correct them.
ls: Teacher plays a short KET-style listening track (3-4 questions) about daily routines, where students listen and tick correct pictures on their paper, checking comprehension of simple present tense.
re: Stand Up Sit Down: Teacher calls out S1 verbs (e.g., 'eat', 'drink', 'walk') and students stand up if they do the action daily, sitting down if not, reactivating vocabulary physically.
prod: Individual speaking interviews: Students take turns with the teacher for 2-3 minutes, answering KET-style questions (e.g., 'What's your job?', 'Where do you live?') while others quietly review S1 flashcards.
rw: Writing Task: Students write 3-5 sentences about their weekend using past simple (e.g., 'I went to the market. I bought bread. I ate with my family.'), with a model sentence on the board for support.
st: Teacher closes with a quick 'Good Job!' clap routine, then says: 'Today you completed your S1 assessment. Well done! Thank you, class.'
g: Teacher calls out S1 words; students mark them on their bingo cards and shout 'Bingo!' when they have a line.
Students act out S1 verbs (e.g., 'shop', 'eat') for others to guess, saying the word when correct.
Two teams race to match S1 word cards to picture cards on the board.
Students use word cards to make correct sentences about S1 topics.
Students quiz each other with S1 questions, then trade cards and find a new partner.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write 5 extra sentences about their favorite S1 topic (e.g., food, shopping).
Support / weaker learners: Use a word bank with S1 verbs to complete the writing task.
hw: Review S1 vocabulary list and write 3 sentences using 3 new words.
Listen to a short English song (e.g., 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes') and write down 5 words they know.
Practice introducing themselves and asking 2 questions (e.g., 'What's your name?', 'Where are you from?') with a family member.
tip: For adults, frame the assessment as a 'progress check' to reduce anxiety; emphasize their growth since S1 began to build confidence.
checklist: Can introduce themselves and ask for personal information
Can ask and answer about daily routines
Can write 3-5 sentences about past events
Can order food in a restaurant
Can make a simple phone call
